name: led
title: LED with series resistor, driven by a signal
about: A GPIO or logic output drives an LED to ground through a series resistor; the resistor sets the current, I = (V_in - Vf) / R.

ports.in: the driving signal: a GPIO or a logic output

components.label: {as}: LED series resistor
components.notes: 150 Ω with this green LED (Vf 2.6 to 3.1 V): about 1.6 to 4 mA from a 3.3 V GPIO, 10 to 15 mA from 5 V – at the high end of Vf it still lights (SIM.state: at least 1 mA). Another current: another value of the same series (part-search skill).

notes: sim.json: the driving net under the MCU's outputs, and leds_on in every load – the LED's designator where it lights, [] or the others where it is dark (SIM.driver); edakit sim then checks the current against the LED and the MCU pin (LIM) and that it lights or stays dark (SIM.state).
From an MCU pin keep the current within the pin's rating (gpio_i_max_a in the MCU's parts entry); for more light a transistor (block npn-switch) or an LED driver.
